paper_summary: This paper investigates the relationships between solar flare properties and the associated coronal mass ejections (CMEs) by extrapolating solar observations to estimate mass and energy losses in active stellar coronae. The authors compile a database spanning 1996–2007 of soft X-ray flares observed by GOES and CMEs measured by LASCO on SoHO to establish power law relationships between flare X-ray fluence and CME mass and kinetic energy, and discuss implications for stellar mass loss and dynamo energy budgets.

instruments.name: Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite (GOES)
instruments.general_comments: GOES is used to observe and record soft X-ray solar flares; its 1–8 Å X-ray band observations provide the X-ray fluence data forming the basis for CME–flare scaling relations over the period 1996–2007.
supporting_quotes: They compiled a database of soft X-ray ﬂares observed by the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite (GOES) that were associated with CMEs observed by the Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph (LASCO) on board the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SoHO) mission.

data_collection_periods.period_name: Solar Flare Observations for CME Scaling
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Soft X-ray flare fluxes, peak X-ray fluence, and integrated X-ray energy
supporting_quotes: Yashiro & Gopalswamy (2009) studied the statistical relationships between solar ﬂares and CMEs observed over the period 1996-2007.
...a good correlation was found between the flare fluence and the CME kinetic energy.
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: GOES observations provide the primary dataset for quantifying solar flare energy, serving as the empirical basis to extrapolate CME behaviors to active stars.

instruments.name: Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph (LASCO) on board the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SoHO)
instruments.general_comments: LASCO is a white-light coronagraph used to image and measure CMEs in the solar corona; its observations are paired with GOES X-ray data to link flare events to the ejected mass and kinetic energy of CMEs over 1996–2007.
supporting_quotes: ...CMEs observed by the Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph (LASCO) on board the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SoHO) mission.

instruments.name: Kepler Photometer (Optical Kepler Photometry)
instruments.general_comments: The Kepler photometer provides optical-band observations of stellar flares; it is referenced for detecting giant flares on solar-type stars that motivate extrapolations of solar CME properties.
supporting_quotes: ...recent giant ﬂare detections on solar-type stars based on optical Kepler photometry by Maehara et al. (2012).

data_collection_periods.period_name: Giant Flare Detections on Solar-type Stars
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Giant optical flares on solar-type stars
data_collection_periods.additional_comments: While not directly used for CME scaling in this paper, Kepler flare detections support the concept of flare-dominated stellar coronae and motivate extrapolation of solar relationships to active stars.
